NOTE 20. 26.09.2025 BVLNC,J  I.A.No.1 of 2023  Heard Smt.Aishwarya Nagula, learned  counsel for the petitioner/appellant and  learned Additional Public Prosecutor  representing the State.

Petitioner is Accused in POCSO  S.C.No.303 of 2019 on the file of the learned  Special Sessions Judge, designated for  Speedy Trial of Offences under Protection of  Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act,
 2012, Ananthapuramu.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the  petitioner/appellant would submit that
petitioner/convict/accused was found guilty for  the offence under Section 376(3) of IPC and Section 5(1) r/w 6 of the POCSO Act, 2012.

He was convicted and sentenced to undergo  rigorous imprisonment for (20) years and to  pay fine of Rs.5,000/- (Rupees five thousand  only) and in default to suffer simple  imprisonment for a period of three months for  the offence U/s.5(1) r/w 6 of POCSO Act,
 2012.
 Contd.,
 2  She would further submit that the date  of offence was on 07.08.2019 even as per the  case of the prosecution.

Therefore, on the  date of offence, the minimum sentence  prescribed under Section 6 of POCSO Act,
 2012, was only ten (10) years, which may  extend to life.

But the learned trial Court  erroneously imposed 20 years of sentence,
 which is not in accordance with law.

The State of  Chhattisgarh and another2 "the minimum  sentence is considered as ten (10) years", the  accused was already undergone 2 years  sentence, and the trial Court erroneously  convicted the petitioner without appreciating  the facts in proper perspective, and there is  no likelihood of taking the appeal for hearing  in the coming days.

No written objections filed by the learned Additional Public Prosecutor opposing the present application, and would submit that it is not a fit case to suspend the sentence.

Further, he would submit that the accused is in prison for the last two years,
four months and he was on bail during the trial, and before, and there are no allegations of breach of bail during the trial and there are no negative antecedents against the appellant.

Considering the above facts and circumstances submitted above, it appears that the date of offence in the case was on 07.08.2019 , on which date, the minimum sentence fixed for the offence was only ten (10) years.

However, the trial Court which delivered the judgment, subsequent to amendment, imposed sentence for twenty (20) years, instead of ten (10) years, which is the minimum sentence at the time of offence.

sentences.text:
There are no negative antecedents against the petitioner from the information provided by the Jail Authorities, as submitted by the learned Contd..
Addl.Public Prosecutor.

In the light of foregoing circumstances and as there is no possibility for taking the appeal for hearing in the near future, "the order of sentence imposed by the learned Special Sessions Judge, designated for Speedy Trial of Offences under Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, 2012,
Ananthapuramu, vide judgment dated 11.08.2023 passed in POCSO SC.No.303 of 2019 be suspended and the petitioner/Accused shall be released on bail, subject to the following conditions:
i) The petitioner/appellant shall be enlarged on bail, on executing a personal bond for Rs.20,000/-
(Rupees Twenty Thousand only), with two (02) sureties for a like sum each, to the satisfaction of the learned Special Court.
ii) On such release, the petitioner/ appellant shall appear before the learned Special Court, on every fourth Saturday of the month, till disposal of the Appeal.
iii) The petitioner/appellant shall not intimidate or annoy the victim and her family members in any manner.
Contd..
iv) The petitioner/appellant shall not leave the country without permission of the Court.
v) The petitioner/appellant shall not involve in similar offence in any manner.
vi) If the petitioner/appellant violates any of the above conditions, the prosecution is at liberty to file an application seeking cancellation of the bail.
Accordingly, this application is ordered.
